title: ATOMS: ALMA three-millimeter observations of massive star-forming regions - VII. A catalogue of SiO clumps from ACA observations
question: What is the nature of SiO emission and shocked gas under different physical conditions and evolutionary stages in massive star-forming regions?

what.value: CS J=2-1 line survey of UC HII regions used for sample selection

evidence.quote: The sample sources were selected from the CS $J$=2-1 line survey of UC Hii regions in the Galactic Plane (cite: bronfman1996cs).

what.value: Basic parameters of the sample sources (distance, clump mass, bolometric luminosity, effective radii, dust temperature)

evidence.quote: The basic parameters of the sample were taken from (cite: liu2020atoms), (cite: liu2020atomsII), and (cite: liu2021atomsIII) ( paper I, paper II, and paper III of the series).

evidence.loc: The line broadening of SiO emission
evidence.quote: $M$ and $R$ the clump mass and effective radii compiled in (cite: liu2020atoms).

recipe.goal: Generate Moment maps and visually identify SiO clumps
recipe.method: Generate Moment 0, Moment 1, and Moment 2 maps of SiO (2-1) using channels with signals > 3 sigma; visually identify SiO clumps in Moment 0 maps and inspect spectra for weak (~2 sigma) clumps.

recipe.goal: Measure SiO clump sizes, positions, integrated intensities, and radii
recipe.method: Fit 2D Gaussians to SiO clumps in Moment-0 maps using CASA imfit; calculate linear radius as geometric mean of major and minor axis FWHM (or use beam size if unresolved).

recipe.goal: Extract spectra and derive line kinematics and outflow classifications
recipe.method: Extract spectra of SiO, HCO+, CS, and H13CO+ over clump size or beam size aperture toward SiO peaks; derive velocity and velocity dispersion from Moment 1 and 2 maps (or 1-component Gaussian fit for 18 weak clumps); smooth SiO and HCO+ to 1.49 km s^-1 to search for high-velocity line wings across SiO, HCO+, and CS.

recipe.goal: Classify clumps by HII region and continuum association and compute physical parameters
recipe.method: Classify clumps into groups A, B, C, D based on spatial coincidence with 3 mm continuum (separation threshold of half beam size) and H40alpha (>3 sigma); compute SiO luminosity L_SiO, shocked gas fraction proxy [SiO]/[H13CO+], and clump particle number density n.
key_parameters: H40alpha detection threshold > 3 sigma; spatial separation threshold = 0.5 beam size
assumptions: Both SiO and H13CO+ emission are optically thin and have constant excitation temperatures; H13CO+ abundance does not vary substantially with time
Mean molecular weight per free particle mu = 2.37

recipe.method: Perform Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) tests, Spearman-rank correlation tests, and linear regressions comparing SiO velocity dispersion, L_SiO, and [SiO]/[H13CO+] against outflow status, HII region association, T_d, n, L_bol, and L_bol/M.

score_reason: Public ALMA project code is stated and complete derived tables (Tables A1-A3) are provided in the text, enabling immediate reproduction of all statistical tests and linear fits; however, full reproduction from visibility/cube data is hindered by subjective 'by eye' clump and outflow wing identification and unstated velocity integration ranges.
rediscovery_reason: All ALMA ACA data are public under 2019.1.00685.S, the catalog of 146 targets and 171 clumps is explicitly tabulated, and the main statistical findings (detection rates, velocity dispersion distributions, L_SiO-L_bol correlations) are quantitative.
